citations.title: Inspection and Licensing of Facilities (adult care homes and family care homes)
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for licensing, resident rights, discharge and appeal, and penalties for ACHs and FCHs. Defines abuse, neglect, exploitation, adult care home, administrator and the adult care home resident discharge team.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines abuse as willful or grossly negligent infliction of pain, injury or mental anguish, unreasonable confinement, or deprivation of needed services by administrator or staff. Also defines neglect, exploitation and personal care.

citations.title: Declaration of residents' rights
citations.requirement: Residents have the right to dignity and privacy and to a written statement of services and charges on admission. They have the right to be free of abuse, neglect and exploitation, to private communication and phone access, and to a copy of this section on admission.

citations.title: Declaration of residents' rights: transfer and discharge
citations.requirement: Discharge only for medical reasons, the resident's or other residents' welfare, nonpayment, or legal mandate. At least 30 days' advance notice except for jeopardy to health or safety. The resident may appeal and stay in the facility until the appeal is resolved unless law provides otherwise.

citations.title: Adult care home resident discharge appeals; resident discharge team
citations.requirement: Basis for resident appeals of ACH discharge notices through the NC Medicaid Hearing Office. Subsection (e) establishes the local adult care home resident discharge team that helps with placement.

citations.title: Medication aide training, skills validation and examination
citations.requirement: ACH staff who administer medications, and their direct supervisors, must complete training and clinical skills validation and pass the written exam. Persons authorized by occupational licensure law to administer medications are exempt.

citations.title: Provisional license; revocation
citations.requirement: Basis for provisional licenses and for revocation under 131D-2.7(b) and 131D-29. A provisional license and the DHSR notice of reasons must be posted in place of the full license.

citations.title: Administrative penalties
citations.requirement: Basis for DHSR penalties on ACHs and FCHs for rule violations. Penalties are listed publicly for the preceding 36 months.

citations.title: Annual license fees (as quoted on DHSR forms)
citations.requirement: Annual license fee: $315 for homes with 6 or fewer beds. $360 plus $17.50 per bed for homes with more than 6 beds. The ACH initial fee conflicts between sources and is unresolved.

citations.title: Respite care in adult care homes and family care homes
citations.requirement: Directs the Medical Care Commission to amend rules on respite care in ACHs and FCHs, effective July 1, 2026. Check for amended rules before offering respite stays.

citations.title: Visitation protocols and resident visitation rights during declared disasters and emergencies
citations.requirement: The Secretary establishes visitation protocols during declared disasters and emergencies. Section 131D-7.2 gives ACH and FCH residents visitation rights during a disaster declaration or emergency. Only the section titles were reviewed.

citations.title: Certificate of Need
citations.requirement: All Certificate of Need requirements must be met before an ACH license application is submitted. Licensed ACH capacity and services must comply with the CON.

citations.title: Adult care home administrator certification criteria
citations.requirement: Sets certification criteria for ACH administrators. Per ACLS guidelines: age 21 or older, 120-hour Administrator-in-Training program, exam, and criminal background check.

citations.title: List of Definitions (ACH)
citations.requirement: Defines aide duty, manager (day-to-day operation in the administrator's absence, per Rule .0402), medication aide (Rule .0403), personal care aide supervisor (Rule .0609), on-call, supervision, responsible person and legal representative. Shifts: 1st 7:01a-3:00p, 2nd 3:01p-11:00p, 3rd 11:01p-7:00a. Eff. 9/1/2024.

citations.title: List of Definitions (FCH)
citations.requirement: FCH definitions, including ambulatory and non-ambulatory, supervisor-in-charge (in the administrator's absence, per Rule .0402), aide duty, medication aide (Rule .0403), supervision, and the same shift hours as 13F. Eff. 9/1/2024.

citations.title: The License (ACH)
citations.requirement: Post the license in a publicly viewable place. Post any provisional license and the DHSR notice of reasons in its place. The license is not transferable. New applications must disclose owners with 5% or more interest. The home is licensed only as an ACH.

citations.title: The License (FCH)
citations.requirement: Post the license in a publicly viewable place. Post any provisional license and the DHSR notice in its place. The license is not transferable. New applications must disclose owners with 5% or more interest.

citations.title: Applying for a License to Operate a Facility Not Currently Licensed (ACH)
citations.requirement: CON first. Packet includes the application, plans, fire marshal report, sanitation report, license fee and certificate of occupancy. Licensure requires ACLS approval of the facility's operational policies and procedures, a pre-licensing survey, and written notice within 14 days of the decision.

citations.title: Applying for a License to Operate a Home Not Currently Licensed (FCH)
citations.requirement: Apply through the county DSS, which submits to DHSR within 10 business days. Packet includes zoning approval letter, photos, floor plans and fee. Licensure requires ACLS approval of the home's operational policies and procedures, a pre-licensing survey, and a 14-day written decision notice.

citations.title: Capacity (ACH)
citations.requirement: Licensed capacity is 7 or more residents. Residents may not exceed the number on the license. Bed capacity and services must comply with the CON.

citations.title: Capacity (FCH)
citations.requirement: Capacity is 2-6 residents, based on the building code and each resident's evacuation capability. The license lists ambulatory and non-ambulatory capacity. Notify ACLS if evacuation capability changes or a non-resident will live in the home. Notify the Construction Section immediately if a resident becomes temporarily non-ambulatory.

citations.title: Change of Licensee (ACH)
citations.requirement: Current licensee gives written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents or responsible persons at least 30 days before a change of licensee. Prospective licensee files the change application, fire and sanitation reports dated within 12 months, and the fee.

citations.title: Change of Licensee (FCH)
citations.requirement: Written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents or responsible persons at least 30 days before a change of licensee. The new licensee files the Change Licensure Application, fire and sanitation reports dated within 12 months, and the fee.

citations.title: Renewal of License (ACH)
citations.requirement: File the renewal annually on a calendar-year basis with the nonrefundable fee. It must disclose ownership and include bed capacity (including any Alzheimer's special care unit) and census data. Uncorrected violations lead to a plan of correction extension, a provisional license, or denial.

citations.title: Renewal of License (FCH)
citations.requirement: File the renewal annually on a calendar-year basis with the nonrefundable fee. It must include ownership disclosure, bed capacity and census data. Uncorrected violations lead to a plan of correction extension, a provisional license, or denial.

citations.title: Notification About Closing of Home (ACH)
citations.requirement: Written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents or responsible persons at least 30 days before closing. The notice states the closing date and the plans for moving residents.

citations.title: Closing of Home (FCH)
citations.requirement: Written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents or responsible persons at least 30 days before closing. The notice states the closing date and the plans for moving residents.

citations.title: Denial or Revocation of License (ACH)
citations.requirement: When a notice of revocation is received, the administrator must tell each resident and responsible person in writing of the notice and its basis within 5 calendar days.

citations.title: Denial and Revocation of License (FCH)
citations.requirement: When a notice of revocation is received, the administrator must tell each resident and responsible person in writing of the notice and its basis within 5 calendar days.

citations.title: Appeal of Licensure Action (ACH)
citations.requirement: The licensee may appeal a licensure action by filing a contested case under G.S. 150B-23, after attempts at informal resolution under G.S. 150B-22.

citations.title: Discharge of Residents (ACH)
citations.requirement: Facility-initiated discharge only for listed reasons (needs cannot be met, improved health, safety or health endangered, nonpayment after written warning, or legal mandate). Written Notice of Discharge with Hearing Request Form is hand delivered the day it is dated, with a copy to the responsible person. Notice is 30 days unless urgent. Includes ombudsman contact and discharge team contact.

citations.title: Discharge of Residents: resident-initiated notice
citations.requirement: The administrator may require up to 14 days' written notice from a resident-initiated discharge. The requirement must be stated in the resident contract. Exceptions apply where delay would jeopardize health or safety. The administrator must also document contacts with possible discharge locations.

citations.title: Discharge of Residents (FCH)
citations.requirement: FCH counterpart to 13F .0702 (title confirmed in the NCAC index). Text was not reviewed; confirm that it mirrors 13F .0702 before copying the discharge procedure.

citations.title: Resident Assessment (ACH)
citations.requirement: Assess each resident within 30 days of admission and annually. Use the DHSR instrument or an equivalent. The assessor must meet Rule .0508, plus training if the facility's own instrument is used. It is a functional assessment of psychosocial, cognitive and ADL status. Also required after a significant change of condition.

citations.title: Resident Assessment (FCH)
citations.requirement: FCH assessment mirrors 13F .0801. The assessor must meet Rule .0508. The assessment is functional and uses the DHSR instrument, which covers diagnoses, medications, self-administration ability, ADLs, mental health history, social history, mood and behavior, nutrition, skin, cognition, and vision and hearing.

citations.title: Resident Care Plan (ACH)
citations.requirement: Develop and implement a resident-centered care plan based on the .0801 assessment, including the resident's care preferences. Keep a copy of the current plan where staff can access it.

citations.title: Medication Administration (ACH)
citations.requirement: Administer per a licensed prescriber's orders. Only staff meeting Rule .0403 may administer or prepare. Pre-pour oral solids only within 24 hours of the dose, never PRN meds. Give within 1 hour before or after the scheduled time. Chart immediately after administration; pre-charting is prohibited. The MAR must be accurate and complete.

citations.title: Medication Administration (FCH)
citations.requirement: The FCH rule is jointly cited with 13F .1004 by ACLS (13F/G .1004). Medications must be administered as ordered and MARs must be accurate. FCH-specific text was not reviewed separately.

citations.title: Medication aide requirements (referenced)
citations.requirement: Rule .0403 sets requirements a medication aide must meet. Referenced in 13F .0102(18) and .1004(b), which allow only staff meeting .0403 to administer or prepare medications. Rule text was not reviewed.

citations.title: Self-Administration of Medications; Medication Storage (titles)
citations.requirement: Titles confirmed in the NCAC index for self-administration and storage of medications. Rule text was not reviewed. Pull the text before writing medication storage, self-administration and controlled-substance procedures.

citations.title: Resident Rights (ACH)
citations.requirement: The ACH must assure that all rights under G.S. 131D-21 are maintained and can be exercised without hindrance.

citations.title: Resident Rights (FCH)
citations.requirement: The FCH must assure that all rights under G.S. 131D-21 are maintained and can be exercised without hindrance.

citations.title: Fire Safety and Emergency Preparedness Plans (ACH)
citations.requirement: Written fire evacuation plan with a floor-plan diagram and evacuation routes. Unannounced fire drills quarterly on each shift. Emergency preparedness plan kept in the facility. If residents are evacuated, report to local emergency management, county DSS and ACLS within 4 hours of the decision, and again within 4 hours of their return.

citations.title: Fire Safety and Emergency Preparedness Plan (FCH)
citations.requirement: FCH counterpart to 13F .0309 (title confirmed in the NCAC full-text index). Includes a fire and evacuation plan and an emergency preparedness plan. Text was not reviewed separately. Confirm paragraph-level requirements before writing FCH drill and evacuation procedures.

citations.title: Housekeeping and Furnishings (ACH)
citations.requirement: Walls, ceilings and floors must be clean, safe and functional. No persistent unpleasant odors. Heating, mechanical, plumbing and fire safety equipment must be kept in safe operating condition. Outside premises must be clean and safe.

citations.title: Fire Alarm System (ACH)
citations.requirement: The fire alarm must transmit automatically to the local fire department dispatch center, directly or through a third-party service. Follow local ordinances. Comply with city and county fire safety requirements.

citations.title: Staffing for Facilities with a Census of 21 or More
citations.requirement: Rule title confirmed in the NCAC full-text index. Per ACLS staffing training (May 2025): 21-40 residents need 16 aide duty hours on 1st and 2nd shifts, and 31 or more need a Personal Care Aide Supervisor (see .0609).

citations.title: Staffing of Licensed Adult Care Homes (ACLS Joint Training, May 2025)
citations.requirement: 7-20 residents: at least one designated staff per shift. 7-12 residents: administrator or manager on site or within 500 ft with two-way communication, and an awake staff member if any resident is disoriented or wanders. 81 or more: administrator on duty 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. Manager must be 21 or older with a HS diploma/GED and 12 CE hours a year.

citations.title: CPR and choking management staff coverage
citations.requirement: At least one staff person on the premises at all times must have completed a CPR and choking-management course within the last 24 months.

citations.title: Family care home administrator approval
citations.requirement: Per ACLS guidelines: FCH administrator approval requires a high school diploma/GED, the State-approved 120-hour AIT program, the Administrator Exam, age 21 or older, and a criminal background check. No renewal fee.

citations.title: Application of Physical Plant Requirements (ACH)
citations.requirement: New construction, additions, alterations and repairs must meet Section .0300. Existing facilities meet the code in effect when licensed or altered. DHSR may grant equivalencies. Resident bedrooms are not permitted on the second floor of certain pre-1984 two-story wood-frame ACHs.

citations.title: TB Test, Medical Examination and Immunizations; Resident Contract, Information on Facility and Resident Register (titles)
citations.requirement: Titles confirmed in the NCAC index. Rule text was not reviewed. Pull the text for the TB, medical exam and immunization requirements and for the required contents of the resident contract and resident register.

citations.title: Personal Care and Supervision; Health Care (titles)
citations.requirement: Titles confirmed (13G .0901 Personal Care and Supervision in the NCAC index; 13F .0902 Health Care in DHSR penalty listings). Rule text was not reviewed. Pull the text for personal care, supervision and physician-notification requirements.

citations.title: Special Care Unit Resident Profile and Care Plan (title)
citations.requirement: Title confirmed in the DHSR fiscal analysis of rule readoptions. Rule text was not reviewed. Pull the text for the Alzheimer's/dementia special care unit profile and care plan, and the rest of Section .1300, before writing memory-care policy.

citations.cite: 2026 NC State Medical Facilities Plan, Policy LTC-3
citations.title: Certification of Beds for Special Assistance
citations.requirement: Applies to CON applicants proposing new ACH beds under a need determination. Covers certification of beds for State/County Special Assistance. SMFP effective 2026-01-01.

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Give medications only per a licensed prescriber's order
Only staff meeting 10A NCAC 13F .0403 may administer or prepare medications; G.S. 131D-4.5B requires training, skills validation and the written exam (licensed professionals exempt)
Administer within 1 hour before or after the scheduled time
Chart immediately after administration; pre-charting is prohibited and the MAR must be accurate and complete
Pre-pour oral solids only within 24 hours of the dose, never PRN medications

policies.title: Medication Storage, Self-Administration, Disposal, Errors and Pharmacy Services
state_specifics: Cover every topic in 10A NCAC 13F/13G .1001-.1010 using DHSR's form 'Guidelines for the Development of Medication Administration Policies and Procedures'
Self-administration (.1005) and storage (.1006) rule text has not been reviewed; pull it before finalizing storage, controlled-substance and disposal steps
The MAR must stay accurate and complete, including for medication errors and refusals

policies.category: Use of physical restraints and alternatives
policies.title: Physical Restraints, Alternatives and Restraint-Free Behavior Management
state_specifics: Document alternatives attempted before any physical restraint
Define the process for orders, consents and documentation, and for assessment and care planning of any restrained resident
A restraint-free home must state its plan to manage and supervise behaviors: alternatives used, resident assessment, communication with physician/responsible person, discharge planning if needed
Unreasonable confinement counts as abuse under G.S. 131D-2.1

policies.title: Accident and Incident Handling, Follow-Up Care and Notification
state_specifics: Notification chain: Administrator/supervisor-in-charge, county DSS, DHSR, family/responsible person
Document resident follow-up care and physician notification
Evacuation-related reporting has its own 4-hour deadline (see FIR-02)

policies.title: Management of Resident Physical Aggression or Assault
state_specifics: Cover aggression toward residents, staff and others
Include staff de-escalation steps, resident separation and assessment
Notify physician and responsible person; consider change-of-condition reassessment
Complete an incident report and follow INC-01 notifications

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Misappropriation: Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: G.S. 131D-2.1 defines abuse as willful or grossly negligent infliction of pain, injury or mental anguish, unreasonable confinement, or deprivation of needed services
Residents have the right to be free of abuse, neglect and exploitation (G.S. 131D-21)
Policy must name the entities notified, including reporting to the Health Care Personnel Registry
Protect the resident, preserve evidence and prohibit retaliation
DHSR administrative penalties (G.S. 131D-34) are published for 36 months

policies.title: Missing Resident: Search and Reporting Procedures
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F .1211(6); 13G .1211
Written search procedure: who searches, areas checked, time limits
Written reporting procedure: when to notify law enforcement, responsible person, county DSS and DHSR
Document the event and post-event reassessment

policies.category: Identification and Supervision of Wandering Residents
policies.title: Identification, Assessment and Supervision of Wandering or Disoriented Residents; Door Alarms
state_specifics: 7-12 residents: at least one staff awake at all times if any resident is disoriented or wanders
Staff report disoriented or wandering behavior to the administrator/supervisor-in-charge; assess behavior changes
Document the supervision plan for each resident
Door alarms and monitoring devices: written testing, operation and maintenance schedule

policies.title: Fire Evacuation Plan, Fire Drills and Life Safety
state_specifics: Written evacuation plan with floor-plan diagram and routes; state where it is posted
Unannounced fire drills quarterly on each shift; document every drill
Fire alarm must transmit automatically to the local fire department dispatch center, directly or via a third-party service
Follow city and county fire safety requirements
FCH rule text (13G .0316) not reviewed separately; confirm paragraph-level requirements

policies.title: Disaster and Emergency Preparedness Plan
state_specifics: Written plan covers at minimum fire, tornado, hurricane and power outage, including special needs sheltering (and transportation for FCHs)
Use the NC Risk Management Portal Licensed Care Facility Risk Management Plan template (rmp.nc.gov/portal)
If residents are evacuated, report to local emergency management, county DSS and ACLS within 4 hours of the decision and again within 4 hours of return
G.S. 131D-7.2 gives residents visitation rights during a disaster declaration or emergency
Keep the plan in the facility

policies.category: Infection Control Procedures in Accordance with CDC Guidelines and Session Law 2011-99
policies.title: Standard Precautions, Hand Hygiene and Glove Use
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F .1211(4); 13G .1211
Define Standard Precautions and when they apply
Handwashing: step-by-step how and when
Gloves: when to use and how to remove properly

policies.category: Infection Control Procedures in Accordance with CDC Guidelines and Session Law 2011-99
policies.title: Bloodborne Pathogens, Sharps Disposal and Staff Exposure Response
state_specifics: Proper disposal of single-use equipment that punctures skin, mucous membranes or other tissue
Disinfection of reusable resident care items used for multiple residents
Blood and bodily fluid precautions
Written steps after staff exposure to blood or body fluids with significant risk of HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C or other bloodborne pathogens

policies.category: Infection Control Procedures in Accordance with CDC Guidelines and Session Law 2011-99
policies.title: Sanitation, Supplies, Infection Control Designee and Compliance Monitoring
state_specifics: Sanitation of rooms and equipment: procedures, agents and schedules
State where infection control devices and supplies are kept for easy staff access
Bar staff with exudative lesions or weeping dermatitis from direct care involving contact until resolved
Designate an on-site staff member knowledgeable in CDC guidelines to direct infection control and train all staff
Procedure for monitoring compliance with the policy

policies.category: Infection Control Procedures in Accordance with CDC Guidelines and Session Law 2011-99
policies.title: Communicable Disease Outbreak Reporting and COVID-19 Protocols
state_specifics: Name who reports suspected communicable disease outbreaks to the local health department
Include COVID-19 protocols: screening, isolation, testing, visitation, reporting
Align with current CDC and NC DHHS guidance

policies.category: Infection Control Procedures in Accordance with CDC Guidelines and Session Law 2011-99
policies.title: Tuberculosis Screening (Two-Step) and Employee Health
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F/13G .0405 (two-step TB testing of residents and staff); 13F .0703 covers TB test, medical exam and immunizations
Describe the process and timing for two-step testing of residents and staff
Rule text for .0703 not reviewed; pull before finalizing medical exam and immunization steps

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Residents or family may file a grievance; define how and with whom
Facility follows up and documents every grievance and its resolution
List outside resources with names and phone numbers: Regional Long-Term Care Ombudsman, county DSS, DHSR Adult Care Licensure Section (919-855-3765)
No retaliation; ombudsman has access to residents

policies.title: Refunds, Deposits and Prepaid Fees
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F .1104/.1105; 13G .1104/.1105 (rule text not reviewed; confirm before finalizing)
State the refund rules in the resident contract
Facility-initiated discharge requires 30 days' notice unless urgent
Resident may be required to give up to 14 days' written notice only if the contract says so
SA residents: do not charge above the state maximum

policies.category: Visitation in Facility & Sign Out Log
policies.title: Visitation and Resident Sign-Out Log
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F .0906; 13G .0906
Maintain a visitor policy and a resident sign-out/sign-in log
Residents have the right to private communication and phone access (G.S. 131D-21)
During declared disasters/emergencies, follow G.S. 131D-7.1 and 131D-7.2 visitation rights

policies.title: Smoking Policy
state_specifics: Designated outdoor smoking areas only; no smoking inside
Ongoing assessment and increased supervision of residents who smoke
State consequences of non-compliance, shared with residents at admission

policies.title: Alcohol Use and Substance Abuse Policy
state_specifics: Assess the resident and communicate with the physician about alcohol use
Safekeep and monitor alcohol only with a physician's order
State consequences of non-compliance with alcohol and substance abuse rules
Include in resident contract and admission orientation

policies.title: Activities Program and Calendar
state_specifics: Official cite: 13F/13G .0905(c)(2)(d)
Sample calendar must meet the required hours and show beginning and end times of each activity
Include a variety of activities and outings
Post the calendar and adapt to resident preferences and assessments

policies.title: Food Service, Menus and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F/13G .0509, .0904(c)(d)
Monthly sample menu must list portion sizes (e.g., 1 cup green beans)
Therapeutic diet menus must be developed by a Registered Dietitian, with RD signature and RD number on each menu
Accommodate dietary needs from the physician's orders and the resident assessment

policies.title: Resident Contract and Admission Agreement
state_specifics: Official cites: 13F .0704; 13G .0704 (contract must include every area listed in the rule)
Written statement of services and charges on admission (G.S. 131D-21), plus a copy of resident rights
A 14-day resident notice requirement must be written in the contract
Contract must be consistent with discharge rules (30-day notice; Hearing Request Form)
SA residents: accept the state rate and no charge above the maximum

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator and Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: Document the operational plan, staffing patterns and the responsibility of each staff member
Manager (replaced 'Administrator in Charge' eff. 9/1/2024): age 21+, HS diploma/GED, 12 CE hours per year
FCH: a supervisor-in-charge acts in the administrator's absence
7-12 residents: administrator or manager in the facility or within 500 ft with two-way communication
81+ residents: administrator on duty 8 hours/day, 5 days/week

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Capacity, Renewal, Change of Licensee and Closure
state_specifics: Post the license publicly; post any provisional license and DHSR notice in its place; license is not transferable
Never exceed licensed capacity (ACH 7+, FCH 2-6); ACH beds must match the CON
Renew annually on a calendar-year basis; renewal discloses ownership, capacity and census; fees: ACH $360 + $17.50/bed, FCH $315 (initial ACH fee conflict unresolved; confirm with ACLS)
Give written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents/responsible persons at least 30 days before change of licensee or closing
On a revocation notice, tell each resident and responsible person in writing within 5 calendar days

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and ACLS Policy Approval
state_specifics: ACLS must approve operational policies and procedures before licensure
FCH: county adult home specialist reviews the operational plan, then submits the packet to DHSR within 10 business days
Annual review with version dates and staff acknowledgment
Update when rules change (e.g., respite care rules under G.S. 131D-6.1 effective 7/1/2026)

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Review incidents, grievances, falls, medication errors and survey findings at least quarterly
Track plans of correction through completion
DHSR penalties for rule violations are published for 36 months
County DSS monitors adult care facilities at least quarterly

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Billing Integrity and Special Assistance/Medicaid Rules
state_specifics: SA residents: facility must agree to the state rate and cannot charge above the SA maximum; resident keeps a $70 personal needs allowance
SA room-and-board is funded 50% state / 50% county; SA recipients are automatically Medicaid-eligible
Adult Care Cost Report next due 9/30/2027; AUP no longer required for 7+ bed facilities beginning on or after 7/1/2026 (S.L. 2026-41)
Beds certified for SA under 2026 SMFP Policy LTC-3 (new CON beds)
Confirm with NC Medicaid whether PCS billing and EVV apply before billing

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Residents' Bill of Rights)
state_specifics: Rights in G.S. 131D-21 must be maintained and exercisable without hindrance (13F/13G .0909)
Give each resident a copy of G.S. 131D-21 on admission
Rights include dignity, privacy, private communication, phone access, and freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation
Post rights and ombudsman contact; train staff annually

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Exploitation and misappropriation of resident property are reportable (see INC-03)
SA residents keep the $70 personal needs allowance
Written receipts and a ledger for any funds held
Resident funds are kept separate from facility funds

policies.title: Advance Directives
state_specifics: Ask about advance directives at admission and place copies in the record
Honor documented wishes and communicate them to hospice, EMS and hospital on transfer
Staff are told where directives are filed

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Residents have the right to privacy and confidential records (G.S. 131D-21)
Privacy notice and minimum-necessary rules for staff
Release of information only with authorization or as law allows (e.g., to DHSR, county DSS, ombudsman)

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: No discrimination in admission or care based on race, color, national origin or disability
Provide interpreters or translated materials for limited-English residents
Provide reasonable accommodations for disabilities
Honor dignity and preferences in care planning

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Admit only when the home can meet the resident's needs within licensed capacity
FCH capacity depends on building code and each resident's evacuation capability (ambulatory vs non-ambulatory)
Medical exam, TB test and immunizations per 13F .0703 (text not reviewed)
Resident contract signed at admission (see CON-01)
Check amended respite care rules (G.S. 131D-6.1) before offering respite stays

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: Assess each resident within 30 days of admission and annually
Reassess after a significant change of condition
Use the DHSR instrument or an equivalent; the assessor must meet Rule .0508
Assessment is functional: psychosocial, cognitive, ADLs, medications, mood/behavior, nutrition, skin, vision/hearing

policies.title: Resident Care Plan
state_specifics: Develop and implement a resident-centered care plan from the .0801 assessment, including the resident's preferences
Keep the current plan where staff can access it
Update after reassessment or change of condition

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Facility-initiated discharge reasons are limited to those in 13F .0702 (needs cannot be met, improved health, safety or health endangered, nonpayment after written warning, legal mandate)
FCH: notify ACLS if evacuation capability changes
Document efforts to meet needs (services, home health, hospice) before initiating discharge
Consult the physician and responsible person

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice; Discharge Appeals
state_specifics: Written Notice of Discharge with Hearing Request Form is hand delivered the day it is dated, with a copy to the responsible person
30 days' notice unless urgent (jeopardy to health or safety)
Include ombudsman and local adult care home resident discharge team contact
Resident may appeal through the NC Medicaid Hearing Office and stay pending appeal unless law provides otherwise
Resident-initiated: up to 14 days' written notice if stated in the contract; document contacts with possible discharge locations. FCH rule 13G .0705 not reviewed

policies.title: Personal Care, Supervision and Resident Services
state_specifics: Provide personal care and supervision per the care plan (13F .0901)
Define aide duty and supervision as in 13F/13G .0102
Describe services and accommodations offered to residents
Rule text for .0901 not reviewed; pull before finalizing

policies.title: Nursing Services and Delegation
state_specifics: Define when a nurse consultant is used (hours are an operator choice, not a rule minimum)
Only licensed nurses may delegate and perform nursing tasks; staff stay within their authorization
Persons authorized by occupational licensure may administer medications without medication aide training

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Significant change triggers reassessment and care plan update
Notify physician and responsible person promptly and document

official.notes:
NC has no single plan-of-operation form. The reviewing documents are two near-identical ACLS desk-review checklists (DHSR/AC 4649 for ACH, DHSR/AC 4648 for FCH, both Rev. 04-2014). The ACLS Licensure Consultant works through each section, checks it off on a blank line, and signs 'Desk review completed. Required policies and procedures have been verified.' The forms do not number their items. Section order is the form's order. The item_ids (1-15, with sub-letters a, b, c... for the checkbox lines) are only ordinal labels I added, and the rule cites are the forms' own.

Process: for the ACH, the Construction Section notifies ACLS of the new project, and ACLS then contacts the applicant for 'the application, policies and procedures.' For the FCH, once ACLS receives the packet from the county adult home specialist, it 'sends a letter to the applicant requesting submission of certain records, policies and procedures for review.' The county adult home specialist also meets the applicant to review the operational plan. The DSS specialist's emphasis areas are doc 2 above. The policies are not submitted with the license application or fee.

Submission: organize the manual in the checklist's section order so each checkbox can be located. Include actual documents where the form asks for them: the fire evacuation plan, the disaster plan, a one-month sample menu with portion sizes (RD-signed therapeutic menus if used), an activity calendar with start and end times, and the resident contract. Medications are covered by the separate optional DHSR Form AC 4640 'Guidelines for the Development of Medication Administration Policies and Procedures', which I did not fetch, so I did not list its content. ACLS also posts an optional Template Infection Prevention & Control Policies and Procedures for ACHs and FCHs (DOCX) on its Forms page, which I did not fetch. The AC 4649/4648 forms are dated 2014 even though the rules were readopted effective 9/1/2024, so the rule cites may have been renumbered. Confirm the current rule numbers with ACLS (919-855-3765) before citing them.
